name: 5mm LED (red)
desc: The classic little light. Needs a resistor in series (220Ω on 5V boards, 100Ω on 3.3V boards) or it burns out.
note: The long leg (+, anode) goes toward the pin, and the short leg (−, flat side) goes to GND.

name: 5mm LED (yellow)
desc: A yellow 5mm LED. Always pair it with a resistor (220Ω on 5V, 100Ω on 3.3V).
note: The long leg (+) goes toward the pin and the short leg (−) to GND.

name: 5mm LED (green)
desc: A green 5mm LED. Always pair it with a resistor (220Ω on 5V, 100Ω on 3.3V).
note: The long leg (+) goes toward the pin and the short leg (−) to GND.

name: 5mm LED (blue)
desc: A blue 5mm LED. It needs about 3V, so on 3.3V boards it glows a bit dimmer. Use 220Ω on 5V and 100Ω on 3.3V.
note: The long leg (+) goes toward the pin and the short leg (−) to GND.

name: 5mm LED (white)
desc: A bright white 5mm LED for lamps and flashlights. It needs about 3V, so it is dimmer on 3.3V boards.
note: The long leg (+) goes toward the pin and the short leg (−) to GND.

name: RGB LED (common cathode)
desc: Three LEDs (red, green, blue) in one, so you can mix any color. This version's shared long leg goes to GND.
variantNote: Common cathode: long leg to GND, and a HIGH pin turns a color ON. One resistor per color leg.

name: RGB LED (common anode)
desc: The same 3-in-1 color LED, but its shared long leg goes to + power, so the code is flipped (LOW = ON).
variantNote: Common anode: long leg to 5V/3.3V, and a LOW pin turns a color ON. One resistor per color leg.

name: WS2812B LED Strip (1m, 60 LEDs)
desc: A strip of 60 color LEDs you can control one by one with a single data wire. Rainbows, room lighting and music visualizers.
variantNote: Strip: 60 LEDs per metre, can be cut between LEDs.
power: Full white can draw up to 3.6A per metre. Use a separate 5V supply (4A for 1m), add a 1000µF capacitor across power and a 330Ω resistor on the data line, and limit brightness in code.

warn.3.3: WS2812B data from 3.3V boards usually works for short runs, but a level shifter (74AHCT125) makes it reliable.

name: WS2812B 8-LED Stick
desc: A short bar of 8 color LEDs, easy to plug into a breadboard. Great for level meters and status bars.
power: Up to ~480mA at full white. USB power is fine if you keep brightness moderate in code.
note: Usually needs header pins soldered on.

name: WS2812B 16-LED Ring
desc: 16 color LEDs in a circle: perfect for clocks, loading spinners, compasses and glowing "reactor cores".
power: Up to ~960mA at full white. Keep brightness low when powered from USB, or use a separate 5V supply.

name: WS2812B 8x8 RGB LED Matrix
desc: 64 color LEDs in a square: pixel art, emoji faces and mini games in full color.
power: Full white can draw ~3.8A. Limit brightness in code (about 20%) on USB, or use a 5V 4A supply.

warn.3.3: WS2812B data from 3.3V boards usually works on short wires; a 74AHCT125 level shifter makes it reliable.

name: WS2812B 16x16 Flexible LED Panel
desc: 256 color LEDs on a bendable panel: scrolling signs, animations and pixel games.
variantNote: 16x16 grid: 256 LEDs, wired in a zig-zag (serpentine) pattern.
power: At full white 256 LEDs can draw over 15A! Use a 5V 4A+ supply, keep brightness low in code and add a 1000µF capacitor.

warn.3.3: Use a 74AHCT125 level shifter on the data line with 3.3V boards.

name: WS2812B LED Strip (144 LEDs/m)
desc: A super-dense strip for smooth light bars, lightsabers and visualizers.
power: Up to ~8.6A per metre at full white. Use a big 5V supply, inject power at both ends and limit brightness.

warn.3.3: Use a 74AHCT125 level shifter on the data line with 3.3V boards.

name: WS2812B 7-LED Jewel
desc: Seven color LEDs in a tiny flower shape: glowing eyes, buttons and jewelry.

name: WS2812B Single LED (breakout)
desc: One addressable RGB LED on a tiny board: one data wire, any color.

name: SK6812 RGBW LED Strip (60/m)
desc: Like WS2812B but with an extra true-white LED in each pixel for nicer room lighting.
note: In code use NEO_GRBW instead of NEO_GRB.
power: Up to ~4.8A per metre at full RGBW. Use a separate 5V supply and limit brightness.

name: 12V LED Strip (white, non-addressable)
desc: A simple bright white strip: all LEDs on together. Great for shelves and under-desk lights.
power: Needs a 12V supply. Dim or switch it with a logic-level MOSFET; connect the supply's GND to the board's GND.

name: IR LED 940nm (5mm, infrared)
desc: An invisible infrared LED: make your project send TV-remote codes. Your phone camera can see it glow.
note: Use a 100Ω resistor for ~30mA, or a transistor for longer range.

name: 1W High-Power LED (star PCB)
desc: A very bright LED on an aluminium heatsink star, for flashlights and lamps.
power: Never drive it from a pin: use a constant-current driver or a MOSFET with a suitable power resistor, and keep it on a heatsink.

name: 12V COB LED Panel
desc: A flat panel of tightly packed LEDs giving smooth, bright light.
power: Needs a 12V supply switched with a logic-level MOSFET. It gets warm: mount it on metal.

name: LED Filament (3V, flexible)
desc: A bendable glowing thread that looks like a vintage bulb filament. Beautiful for gifts and signs.
power: Draws ~100mA: switch it with a transistor (2N2222 + 1kΩ) and use a series resistor (e.g. 22Ω at 5V).

name: Traffic Light LED Module (with resistors)
desc: Red, yellow and green LEDs on a little board with resistors already built in. Just 4 wires.
